notes.meaning: Children naturally copy their parents, and believers are told to imitate God as His dearly loved children. Because God has shown such great kindness in forgiving our sins, we should reflect His character by forgiving and caring for others. Walking in His footsteps shows that we truly belong to His family.

Believers are called to live their whole lives guided by love, following the pattern Jesus set for us. Christ showed the greatest love possible by giving up His life in our place. His death was an acceptable sacrifice to God, pleasing the Father just like the sweet fragrance of incense.

Sexual sins, impure living, and greedy desire have no place in the lives of God's holy people. These vices are so destructive and shameful that Christians should not even make them topics of casual conversation. Keeping away from such talk helps believers stay pure in heart and conduct.

Coarse speech, empty chatter, and vulgar joking do not fit the character of a Christian. While cheerful conversation is good, corrupt jokes and double meanings poison the mind. Instead of using words for dirty humor, believers should use their tongues to thank and praise God.

Paul gives a solemn warning that anyone who stubbornly lives in sexual sin, impurity, or greed has no share in God's eternal kingdom. Greed is called idolatry because a greedy person puts trust and joy in money rather than in God. Those who continually chase after worldly lusts prove that they do not belong to Christ.

Believers must not let smooth talkers trick them into thinking that sexual sins or greed are harmless mistakes. God takes sin very seriously, and His anger will surely fall on those who practice rebellion and refuse to obey Him. Knowing this judgment protects Christians from making excuses for evil.

Christians must not join in partnership with those who live sinful lives. Sharing in their wicked deeds means taking their side against God and risking the same punishment. Believers must choose their close companions and activities with care.

Before coming to Christ, believers were completely in the dark about God and lived in spiritual ignorance. But now through union with the Lord, they have been transformed into light. Because of this complete inward change, their daily lives should shine with holiness and honesty.

Living in the light produces good fruit in every part of a person's life. This fruit shows up as real kindness toward others, fair and upright dealing, and honest sincerity. Wherever the light of God is active, these good qualities naturally grow.

Children of light must test their thoughts and actions to find out what truly brings pleasure to the Lord. Instead of following the habits of the world, Christians study God's word and put it into practice. Living to please God is the great goal of every true believer.

Christians are commanded to stay completely clear of sinful deeds, which produce no good fruit and only lead to destruction. Merely avoiding evil is not enough; believers are also called to expose and confront it. They do this by speaking the truth and living pure lives that make wickedness obvious.

The sinful deeds that ungodly people do under cover of darkness are deeply disgusting. Such acts are so vile that it is shameful for a Christian even to describe them in detail. Exposing sin does not mean dwelling on filthy topics, but pointing out that they violate God's holy law.

When light shines into dark corners, it reveals the true nature of everything hidden there. In the same way, the light of God's word strips away excuses and shows wicked deeds for what they really are. Once evil is brought into the open, sinners have the opportunity to see their need for mercy and turn to God.

This urgent message calls on people who are asleep and dead in their sins to wake up and turn to God. Spiritual slumber leaves people blind to their eternal danger. But when a sinner stirs and seeks the Lord, Christ promises to shine His bright life, truth, and pardon into their heart.

Believers must pay close attention to how they walk, which means how they conduct their daily lives. Fools wander without thought or purpose and fall into temptation, but wise people guide their steps by God's truth. Walking wisely means living with great care and reverence under God's watchful eye.

Paul urges Christians to buy up every good opportunity, making the most of their precious time. The days are described as evil because the surrounding world is full of wickedness, distraction, and danger. A faithful Christian treats time as a gift from God that must not be wasted on worthless pursuits.

Believers are warned not to be thoughtless or senseless about their spiritual duties. The greatest wisdom is to discover and understand what the Lord wants us to do in every situation. Knowing God's will keeps us safe from the traps of the world.

Getting drunk on wine leads to reckless, wasteful living and breaks down all self-control. Instead of seeking false joy in alcohol, Christians are commanded to let their hearts and minds be continually filled and controlled by the Holy Spirit. The Spirit gives believers true joy, strength, and courage without any harmful effects.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Some scholars note that the phrase can be translated 'filled by the Spirit', meaning that Christ uses the Holy Spirit as the means to fill believers with the fullness of God.

notes.meaning: A heart filled with the Holy Spirit overflows with joyful, sacred music. Christians are encouraged to build one another up by singing the Psalms of Scripture, hymns of praise, and spiritual songs. This music must not be a mere outward show, but must come from sincere devotion directed to the Lord.

Believers are called to give thanks to God the Father at all times and for all things, trusting that He works everything for their good. Even in hard trials, Christians can praise Him for His wisdom and love. All our prayers and praises must be offered in the name and authority of the Lord Jesus Christ.

Paul introduces the duties of household life by urging believers to yield to one another in humble service. This willingness to submit does not come from fear of man, but from deep reverence and love for Christ. Honouring Christ leads Christians to lay aside pride and serve their neighbors.

differ.view: Mutual submission is seen as a universal rule that removes traditional authority ranks between husbands and wives.
Mutual submission introduces an orderly pattern where believers submit to those placed over them in specific callings, such as wives to husbands.

notes.meaning: Wives are directed to submit to their own husbands as a service offered directly to the Lord. A Christian wife does not obey out of slavish fear, but out of devotion to Christ, who established this order in the family. By respecting her husband, she honors the Lord who placed him in that role.

The husband is named the head of the wife, just as Christ is the head of the church. However, Christ holds a unique glory that no human husband can match, because He alone is the Savior who redeemed His body. A husband's leadership should mirror Christ by protecting, providing for, and guiding his wife with gentle care.

Just as the church gladly yields to the authority of Christ, wives should submit to their husbands in all lawful matters. This submission is limited by God's higher law, meaning a wife must never follow a husband into sin. Where God's commands are not violated, she honors the marriage by supporting her husband's leadership.

Husbands are commanded to love their wives with the same deep, self-giving love that Christ showed when He died for the church. A husband's authority must never turn into harshness or selfish rule. Instead, he must be willing to sacrifice his own comfort, ease, and even his life to care for his wife and support her spiritual good.

Christ gave Himself up for the church in order to sanctify her, which means to set her apart as holy for God. He cleanses His people through the inward washing symbolized by water, applying the promises of His word to their souls. This cleansing removes the guilt and power of sin through faith in the gospel.

differ.view: The washing refers directly to the spiritual cleansing worked by the blood of Christ and the word, not to water baptism.
The washing refers to baptism, which conveys real inward and spiritual grace when received with faith.
The washing refers to baptism as an outward sign and seal of God's inward cleansing, though the physical water itself does not cleanse the soul.
The washing is an unquestionable reference to the sacrament of baptism working through the divine word.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: The washing is understood as the sacrament of baptism, with 'the word' often referring to the spoken baptismal formula.

notes.meaning: Christ's great purpose is to present the church to Himself on the last day as a glorious, radiant bride. In that heavenly kingdom, she will have no stain of sin, no wrinkle of decay, and no defect whatsoever. Everything that disfigures believers in this life will be washed away, leaving them completely pure and blameless.

Husbands are called to love their wives just as they love their own physical bodies. Because husband and wife are united into one flesh, caring for her is truly caring for himself. A man who mistreats his wife is acting against nature and destroying his own peace.

No healthy person hates his own flesh; instead, he provides food to nourish it and clothes to cherish and keep it warm. In the very same way, Christ constantly supplies, comforts, and guards His church. Husbands should show that same tender attention to all the needs of their wives.

Christ cares for the church so tenderly because believers are real, living members of His body. We are joined to Him in an intimate spiritual union that shares in His very life. This bond is even closer than the physical relationship between family members on earth.

Paul quotes the creation story from Genesis, where God declared that a man must leave his father and mother to cleave to his wife. While marriage does not cancel love for parents, it creates a new bond that is closer than any other earthly relationship. By God's design, the two are joined together as one flesh.

The union between a husband and a wife points to a great mystery, which is a divine truth once hidden but now revealed. Paul explains that his primary focus is the spiritual union between Christ and His church. Earthly marriage serves as a picture of how the Son of God joins Himself to redeemed humanity.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Because the Latin Vulgate translated the word 'mystery' as 'sacrament', the Catholic Church historically recognizes marriage as one of the seven holy sacraments.

notes.meaning: Paul brings the deep teaching about Christ and the church right back to daily family life. Every individual husband must love his wife with the same warmth and dedication he gives to himself. At the same time, every wife must honor, appreciate, and respect her husband.
